content.title: About
content.content: Carp is a freshwater fish of the family Cyprinidae, widely found in rivers and lakes across Europe and Asia. It has firm flesh, a mildly sweet flavor, and distinctive large scales. Carp is used in both traditional and modern cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Carp can grow over 1.5 m in length and weigh more than 30 kg.
In some cultures carp is a symbol of luck and is featured in New Year dishes.
Carp can survive low‑oxygen conditions by breathing through its skin.
Aquaculture farms raise carp in intensive systems to provide a steady supply.
Male carp develop bright red breeding tubercles during the spawning season.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Carp meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: The fish contains polyunsaturated fats that support heart and vascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Carp supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It offers phosphorus, selenium, and potassium, important for bones, antioxidant protection, and blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Low mercury content
items.content: Compared with many marine fish, carp typically contains less mercury, making it a safer choice.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including carp.

items.title: Parasite contamination
items.content: Raw or undercooked carp can harbor parasites; proper cooking is recommended.

items.title: High sodium in cured preparations
items.content: Traditional methods such as salting or smoking can increase the salt content.

items.title: Environmental concerns
items.content: Intensive carp farming may affect water quality and biodiversity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Carp is commonly baked, fried, boiled, or made into fish cakes. Fillets can be added to salads, soups, and stews. When cooking, it is important to remove bones and skin.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh carp should be kept in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C for no more than 2 days. Frozen carp can be stored at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Before cooking, rinse and pat the fish dry.
